issues.detail: The Greek 'εν χριστω ιησου' (in Christ Jesus) is a prepositional phrase describing the state of the churches. The Vietnamese translation 'trong Đấng Christ và Chúa Giê-xu' (in the Lord Christ and Jesus) incorrectly treats 'Christ' and 'Jesus' as two separate entities/titles joined by 'and' (và), whereas the Greek uses them as a single compound title.

The Greek 'υμεις γαρ' (for you) is at the beginning of the sentence. The Vietnamese translation moves this to the middle/end of the clause ('vì anh em cũng đã...'), though the meaning is largely preserved, the causal link 'for' is slightly shifted in structure.
